metadata.mechanics: This 20 minute procedure requires two Targets - a donor and recipient, both of whom must be willing. Completion causes the donor Target to lose 1 Infection, while the recipient Target gains 1 Infection  and gain 1 Fracture. The recipient's Fracture should manifest as minor personality traits from the person donating the Infection. This procedure does not allow a person to exceed or increase their Infection Pool.
metadata.notes: Any effect which would prevent the loss of the donor's Infection from this procedure also prevents the recipient from gaining an Infection from it.
metadata.descriptionOfRoleplay: There are certain ways to torture someone, and this is one of the worst. Each subject is normally strapped to a table to keep them from flailing wildly. Then, both subjects have their chest cut open and their ribs cracked apart to expose their hearts. The individual conducting the procedure then removes tissue from the donor and begins transplanting it into the one receiving the Infection – pieces of heart, lung, bone, and sinew. Finally, when the trauma is greatest – which causes the Infection to be more easily removed – the donor’s skull is cracked open and their brain exposed. While the recipient heals, the donor find the inability to heal as they are cut – again and again. Many individuals who conduct this procedure find that making the trauma as terrible as they can for the donor allows for the Infection transfer to go more smoothly, since there is a link between Infection, harvesting it, and trauma.
